enrichVolcano

Figures from enrichment results you have already computed: fgsea, clusterProfiler, limma’s fry and camera, over-representation, or your own.

enrichVolcano starts from differential-abundance results you already have and ends in enrichment figures:

library(enrichVolcano)

study <- read_study("my_study.xlsx")
res <- run_enrichment(study, load_gene_sets(c("Hallmark", "GO Slim")))
volcano_ring(study$da, res$fgsea, contrast = "Aging")
  1. read_study() reads your DA results, and optionally the matrix, sample sheet and contrasts, from one workbook; as_da() reads a single DA table from limma, limpa, proteoDA, MSstats, proDA, msqrob2, prolfQua or ProtRank.
  2. run_enrichment() runs fgsea, camera and fry, or as_enrichment() converts enrichment you computed elsewhere. Either way you get a validated enrichment object that records which test produced it.
  3. dedup() (optional) flags redundant terms so a figure shows each signal once. p-values are never changed.
  4. A plot function draws from the object: volcano_ring() for one contrast, volcano_ring_grid() for several, nes_scatter() to compare two contrasts term by term (concordance or reversal).

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Dustyn-T-Lewis/enrichVolcano")

What goes in

Tool Recognised by Score drawn
fgsea its columns NES
clusterProfiler gseaResult its class NES
limma fry, mroast their columns signed −log10(FDR)
limma camera, cameraPR enrichment_test = signed −log10(FDR)
over-representation (enrichR, enrichGO, …) enrichment_test = "ora" + a direction column signed −log10(padj)
anything else enrichment_test = "custom" + column names yours

fry, mroast and camera report no effect size or leading edge, so their score is the signed −log10(FDR) and the legend says so.

What the ring shows

  • Centre: the volcano, logFC against −log10(p).
  • Ring: one arc per term, up-regulated on top and down-regulated below. Fill is the score; height is −log10(padj) for NES and set size otherwise.
  • Ticks: spokes from each arc to its leading-edge genes in the volcano.

By default the ring draws the twelve most significant terms, in either direction, from every collection in the object. For figures, databases = c("Hallmark", "GO Slim") is the recommended view; n_terms, term_threshold and terms change the selection further. vignette("enrichVolcano") walks every step on the bundled example, including how to get each gene-set collection.

Cite the methods you used

Cite the methods behind your results, whether enrichVolcano ran them or you did:

  • limma: Ritchie ME et al. 2015, Nucleic Acids Res 43(7), doi:10.1093/nar/gkv007
  • fgsea: Korotkevich G et al., bioRxiv, doi:10.1101/060012
  • clusterProfiler: Wu T et al. 2021, The Innovation 2:100141
  • camera: Wu D, Smyth GK 2012, Nucleic Acids Res 40(17), doi:10.1093/nar/gks461
  • fry and mroast (ROAST): Wu D et al. 2010, Bioinformatics 26(17), doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btq401
  • EnrichmentMap (dedup()): Merico D et al. 2010, PLoS ONE 5(11):e13984
  • Hallmark gene sets: Liberzon A et al. 2015, Cell Systems 1(6), doi:10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004
  • Enrichment protocol: Reimand J et al. 2019, Nat Protoc 14:482-517

Versioning

1.0.0 replaced the column-name arguments with the enrichment object, and 1.1.0 added the study readers and run_enrichment(); see NEWS.md. Earlier releases stay installable from their tags.
